title: Silicon interposer fused with deep-trench DRAM banks
idea: Combine the passive 2.5D interposer under GPU+HBM with memory: fill its 2,000-3,000 mm2 with 40-65 nm deep-trench eDRAM (AR ~80) plus interposer-native refresh and sense logic, so the wiring substrate is also a multi-GB near-memory tier.
why: Capital intensity (fact 4) and HBM shortage: uses depreciated legacy fabs, no EUV; ~2,500 mm2 at ~0.06 um2/bit gives ~3-5 GB per package at mm-scale wire lengths (fact 5).

title: Display backplane fab fused with DRAM: panel-scale memory sheets
idea: Combine an oxide-TFT display backplane line (3 m Gen-10.5 glass, ~1.5 um rules, a storage capacitor already in every pixel) with DRAM: print 4 stacked tiers of 1T1C cells with small local subarrays, then dice the panel into capacity-tier CXL memory sheets.
why: Cost per bit and capital (fact 4): display area costs ~100x less per m2 than DRAM wafers; ~14 um2/bit x 4 tiers gives ~360 GB raw per panel, targeting <$2/GB for a 100-300 ns capacity tier.

title: Backside power network fused with DRAM periphery
idea: Borrow logic backside power delivery for DRAM: move VPP/VARY/VDD rails and charge-pump capacitors to the wafer backside through nano-TSVs, freeing frontside metal for 2x bitline/local-IO tracks and letting row-decoder strips tuck under the mats.
why: Periphery (fact 7) and voltage floor (fact 10): periphery area -20-30%, lower IR drop allows tighter VARY margins; die area per bit -10-15%.

title: Bonded SRAM sector buffers fused with segmented wordlines
idea: Hybrid-bond a thin SRAM/logic layer so each 1 Kb wordline segment has its own SRAM sector buffer at the bond site; an activate opens only one 64-bit segment and the buffer serves column hits, merging row buffer, cache and wordline segmentation.
why: Overfetch (fact 8): activation energy per useful bit drops ~8-10x (about 5.9 to ~0.7 pJ); fewer full-row activations also lowers hammer exposure (fact 9).

title: Wafer bonding fused with monolithic tiers: four wafers of 32
idea: Combine both 3D routes: each wafer carries a 32-tier monolithic memory stack (aspect ratio manageable in one etch), and four such wafers are hybrid-bonded to one periphery wafer, giving 128 tiers without a 128-tier etch.
why: 3D break-even (fact 2, ~26+ tiers): reaches 128 tiers with 4 moderate etches; etch AR stays <40:1, raising yield and cutting high-AR etch tool time.

title: Capillary self-alignment fused with hybrid die-to-wafer bonding
idea: Pattern hydrophilic bond-pad fields and hydrophobic die rims so a thin water film self-centers each DRAM die to <0.5 um by surface tension before Cu-Cu bonding, letting fast, simple US-built pick-and-place replace imported precision hybrid bonders.
why: HBM stacking (fact 6) and US manufacturability: ~10x throughput and ~5x lower tool cost than precision die-to-wafer bonders made abroad; supports 16-24-high domestic stacks.

title: Eliminate the separate memory die: DRAM on the logic backside
idea: Use the silicon freed by backside power delivery under a logic die to build a trench-capacitor DRAM array, connected to the frontside cache controllers by nano-TSVs at ~1 um pitch.
why: Data movement: memory sits 10 um under the cores, giving <0.5 pJ/bit access and removing a separate die, package and interposer for the first few GB.

title: Electrochromic tiers with plasmonic readout for read-mostly AI weights
idea: Electrochromism: WO3 nanocells, colored or bleached by proton intercalation, keep their state with no power. Each cell sits on a plasmonic nanoantenna whose resonance shift a bonded photodiode array reads optically, a whole page in parallel. Writes are slow (µs) but reads are fast, which suits model weights that are written rarely.
why: Takes read-mostly AI weight capacity off DRAM and removes per-read data movement (facts 5 and 8); claim page-parallel optical reads at tens of fJ/bit with non-volatile storage.

title: Undiced wafer-scale DRAM face-bonded to a wafer-scale accelerator
idea: Jump from die to wafer: keep the 300-mm DRAM wafer whole, use programmable links stitched at each reticle boundary to route around dead mats, and hybrid-bond it face-to-face to a wafer-scale compute wafer so each compute tile gets a multi-GB slab directly above it. No dicing kerf, packages, TSVs or PHYs.
why: Removes the HBM TSV and package tax (fact 6) and data-movement energy (fact 5): ~0.1 pJ/bit vertical access versus 3-4 pJ/bit for HBM.

title: One line mask, rotated 90 degrees, makes 4F2 crosspoints
idea: Use a single SAQP mandrel mask twice: expose it, then rotate the wafer 90 degrees and expose it again on a second hardmask, so its lines define both the wordline and bitline grids and their intersections self-align the vertical-channel pillars of a 4F2 cell.
why: Litho/EUV (fact 4) and density: 4F2 (+33% bits/area) with one shared critical mask instead of two, and perfect pitch match between wordline and bitline grids.

title: Woven tiers: alternate bitline direction 90° to dilute row hammer
idea: Inverts 'a row's neighbors are fixed parallel rows.' Rotate line orientation by 90 degrees on alternate tiers so a hammered row's nearest neighbors above and below are orthogonal lines that each share only one cell with it, spreading aggressor coupling over many victims.
why: Fact 9: disturbance per victim per activation drops ~16-64x, lifting the effective hammer threshold well above 1k.

title: Balanced-layup tiers: alternating stress plies cancel 3D wafer bow
idea: Composite laminates avoid warp with symmetric, balanced layups; design each 3D DRAM tier pair with opposite-sign film stress (tensile channel ply, compressive wordline ply) and orthogonal line directions, so stress and anisotropy cancel every two tiers instead of accumulating.
why: Wafer bow and overlay distortion cap tier count (fact 2); balanced plies could allow 2-3x more tiers before bow limits, well past the ~26-tier break-even.

title: Post-tensioned tendons: one through-stack via fill for N tiers
idea: Precast bridge segments are stacked with aligned ducts and one tendon is threaded through; stack thinned tier wafers with pre-opened, tapered, aligned ducts made by relaxed trailing litho, then one electroplating step fills a continuous via through every tier.
why: Replaces N separate TSV reveal-and-fill sequences with one, cutting HBM TSV cost and yield loss (fact 6); tapered ducts tolerate misalignment.

title: Decal capacitors: high-temperature forest transferred onto transistors
idea: Like a water-slide decal, build the capacitor forest on a donor wafer at 600-800 C, allowing crystalline rutile TiO2 or SrTiO3 (k ~80-150), then bond it upside-down onto a finished access-transistor wafer and remove the donor, so the dielectric never meets the transistor's thermal limit.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1): k ~100 directly meets the k ~70 requirement; claims 2x Cs at half the aspect ratio (AR ~35).

title: Uncut wafer-scale DRAM bonded whole to wafer-scale logic
idea: IFR: 'no dicing, no packages, no interposers.' Backward: never dice the DRAM wafer; stitch a redundant mesh across reticle boundaries, disable bad reticles at test, and wafer-to-wafer bond the whole DRAM wafer onto a wafer-scale processor.
why: HBM tax and data movement (facts 5, 6): no base dies, interposers or stack yield loss; ~3-4 TB of memory at <0.5 pJ/bit on one bonded pair.

title: Diatom-style peptide biosilica grows high-AR scaffolds at 25 C
idea: Mimic diatom silaffin peptides: graft polyamine catalysts onto sidewalls of a shallow patterned template so silica deposits only there from dilute silicic acid at room temperature, iteratively growing tall thin walls/tubes that serve as capacitor molds directly over finished CMOS.
why: Capital and thermal budget of 3D BEOL stacking: plasma-free room-temperature mold growth replaces thick oxide deposition plus 70:1 etch, cutting etch-tool time and energy.

title: Liquid-nitrogen floating-body tiers for a pooled cryogenic memory
idea: TRIZ #35 Parameter changes: run a stacked 1T floating-body array at 77 K inside an LN2-immersed rack-level memory pool, where SRH generation and GIDL fall by ~10^6-10^8. Stored hole states then persist for minutes and steeper subthreshold slopes allow ~0.5 V operation.
why: Fact 3 and 10: refresh effectively disappears and CV2 energy falls ~4x; capacitorless ~4F2 cells, provided cooling overhead stays below the energy saved.

title: Inter-tier metal planes double as shared back gates
idea: TRIZ #6 Universality: in a stacked thin-Si floating-body array, make the conductive plane between tiers do two jobs: it shields tier from tier and is the negative-biased back gate for both the tier above and the tier below, holding stored holes at the back interface. One deposited film replaces a separate back-gate layer per tier.
why: Fact 1 and 2: double-gate capacitorless cells with no extra back-gate layers; ~10x retention vs single-gate floating body and ~30% thinner tier pitch.

title: Merchant pre-grown superlattice starter wafers for capacitorless 3D DRAM
idea: TRIZ #10 Preliminary action: a U.S. epitaxy house pre-grows and sells standardized 64-tier in-situ-doped Si/SiGe superlattice 300 mm wafers with certified defect maps, the way SOI wafers are sold today. Capacitorless 3D cell makers (floating-body, thyristor, gain-cell) start from a finished stack instead of owning epi reactors.
why: Capital intensity and U.S. manufacturability: entrants skip ~$1B of epitaxy capex and months of tier-growth cycle time; creates a new domestic supply-chain node.

title: 77 K floating-body 3D array with hour-scale retention
idea: Shift the thermal timescale: at 77 K (LN2 immersion at rack scale) thermal-generation leakage falls by >10^6, so a capacitorless floating-body cell in stacked thin silicon tiers holds charge for hours. The array is designed only for cryogenic racks and needs neither a capacitor nor refresh.
why: Removes the capacitor wall (fact 1) and refresh (fact 3); enables capacitorless 3D at ~4F2 per tier.

title: Self-ordered anodic alumina pores as litho-free capacitor molds
idea: TRIZ #31 Porous materials, resolving 'taller capacitor vs. costlier etch': sputter ~3 um Al over the storage-node landing pads and let the pad topography seed pore nucleation. Anodizing then grows self-ordered 20-25 nm pores straight down at AR >150:1 in minutes; thin the barrier at the pore bottoms and ALD TiN / high-k / TiN into the pores, keeping the alumina as the mechanical support lattice.
why: Fact 1 and 4: AR ~115-150 without high-AR plasma etch or a capacitor-hole litho layer; ~1.5-2x Cs (or same Cs at ~30% smaller footprint) and removes one of the costliest etch modules.

title: Myelin air-gap sheaths between wordline planes shrink tier pitch
idea: Myelin lets axons be thin yet fast by insulating them; deposit sacrificial carbon layers between the wordline plates of a 3D DRAM stack and ash them out through vent slits after the stack is built, leaving pillar-supported k=1 air gaps between planes.
why: 3D layer count and height: WL-to-WL coupling and disturb fall ~3-4x, so tier pitch can shrink ~30-40%, giving more tiers per micron of etch depth.

title: Solar chemical-bath deposition grows channels in thousand-wafer tanks
idea: Borrowed from thin-film solar, where CdS/ZnO buffer layers grow from warm aqueous baths in huge batches: grow the ZnO/InZnO channel and Al2O3 gate liner inside 256-tier vertical holes by self-limiting chemical bath deposition, ~1,000 wafers per tank instead of single-wafer ALD.
why: ALD/CVD dominates 3D memory capex; a ~$1M bath line replaces ~$100M of ALD, cutting the channel module ~100x and pulling total cost per GB toward the 100x target; trade-offs: lower mobility, more refresh.

title: Peroxide-soluble germanium tiers replace SiGe sacrificial layers
idea: Substitute SiGe sacrificial tiers (normally released with HF/H2O2/acetic or CF4 remote plasma) with Ge-rich tiers (sputtered a-Ge in deposited oxide-semiconductor stacks, thin strained Si0.3Ge0.7 in epi stacks) that dissolve in warm dilute H2O2 as soluble GeO2, selectivity to Si >100:1, opening lateral cavities for capacitors and gate-all-around access devices.
why: Water-based release for 3D DRAM lateral devices (fact 2); higher selectivity permits thinner sacrificial tiers, so more tiers per um of stack.

title: Two-faced wafer: front and back arrays form each differential bitline pair
idea: TRIZ #17 Another dimension: build array plus sense amps on the front, carrier-bond, thin to ~5 um and build a mirror array on the backside at low temperature, joined by nano-TSVs at each sense amp. Each sense amp compares a front bitline with the geometrically identical back bitline, so open-bitline noise mismatch disappears and both faces share one periphery.
why: Fact 7 and resource axis: ~2x bits per wafer start and per quartz-crucible-grown wafer with one set of sense amps; periphery share per bit falls from ~49% toward ~30%.

title: Indium-free zinc-tin-oxide tiers revived for recyclable 3D DRAM
idea: Zinc tin oxide (ZTO) transistors lost to IGZO on mobility and etch control. 3D DRAM access devices need low leakage more than mobility, so use ZTO channels for the stacked tiers, with an all-oxide stack chosen so zinc and tin are recovered by a simple acid leach.
why: Avoids indium (China-dominated, scarce) in oxide-channel 3D DRAM (facts 2, 3), with a recycling route designed in.

title: Stand DRAM dies on edge: TSV-free sideways HBM
idea: Rotate the HBM stack 90 degrees: bond thin core dies into a block, saw and polish one face so every die's edge exposes its top-metal lines, then hybrid-bond that polished edge face directly onto the logic die. Each die talks through thousands of edge wires along its 10 mm edge instead of TSVs.
why: HBM TSV tax (fact 6): removes TSV keep-out area and TSV yield loss; 1-2 um edge pitch gives 5,000-10,000 lines per die; heat conducts along die planes into the base.

title: Trehalose glass: vitrified nanolaminate dielectrics resist decade-long crystallization
idea: Tardigrades and resurrection plants vitrify trehalose into a glass that will not crystallize when hot; build the tier capacitor and inter-tier insulators from Al2O3/HfO2/La2O3 nanolaminates with sublayers below crystallization thickness so they stay amorphous through 10 yrs at 125 C, with no grain boundaries forming as leakage paths.
why: Prevents slow crystallization and grain-boundary leakage growth that degrade retention over life at temperature, at some cost in k.

title: Epitaxial superlattice edges replace EUV for wordline pitch definition
idea: Substitute EUV/SAQP for the densest line layers with superlattice nanowire pattern transfer: grow a 512-period Si/Si0.7Ge0.3 superlattice (6/6 nm), cleave and polish its edge, recess SiGe with peracetic-acid etchant, evaporate Mo at glancing angle onto the Si ridges, and stamp the 512-wire, 12 nm-pitch array onto the target wafer, one stamp per sub-array mat.
why: Litho-bound scaling (fact 4): pitch set by epitaxy (+/-0.3 nm) not a scanner, deleting several EUV/SAQP passes per WL/BL layer while avoiding fluorinated resists and spacer etches.

title: Reactor-robot vacuum-gap access transistors for near-zero off-current
idea: Robots inside reactors use vacuum electronics because vacuum has no lattice to damage; make each access device a vertical nanoscale vacuum-channel transistor, a ~10 nm emitter tip facing a collector inside a ring gate, sealed in its 4F2 pillar when the tier is capped. With no conducting medium, off-state current is only zero-bias field emission, essentially nothing.
why: Leakage tail and refresh (fact 3) eliminated, radiation-immune, and tiny capacitors become viable (fact 1); claim retention of hours.

title: Vacuum-channel field-emission nanotriode as stacked access device
idea: Field emission: each tier's access device is a 10 nm sacrificially formed vacuum gap between a sharp emitter tip and a collector. A gate electrode modulates the Fowler-Nordheim emission, and with zero field the vacuum carries no current at all.
why: Removes the leakage tail (fact 3) with no moving parts, unlike NEMS switches, and is temperature-insensitive for stacking on logic; claim refresh cut by >10x.

title: Minify substrate, magnify layers: fold one memory sheet 32 times
idea: Make one long thin-film memory array on 10 um polyimide through a flexible-TFT foundry shuttle, then fold it accordion-style 32 times, with fold lines carrying edge interconnects to a controller.
why: Layer count by folding instead of tier deposition: tests a no-bonding 3D path for under $300k. Density per layer is low, so it is a moonshot demo.

title: Vertical domain-wall racetracks lining deep holes like 3D NAND
idea: Current-induced domain wall motion: Co/Ni multilayer racetracks deposited on the sidewalls of deep vertical holes store 32-64 magnetic domains per hole. A spin-orbit-torque Pt liner shifts the domains to a single read/write MTJ at the hole base.
why: Gives non-volatile storage with many bits per 4F2 footprint and almost no periphery per bit (facts 2 and 7); claim 10-30x density per footprint with ns shifts.

title: Cross-shaped four-way cells around every vertical bitline
idea: Limit: vertical bitline holes cannot get denser. Slice each tier around a vertical bitline into four quadrant channels, so one bitline serves four lateral cells per tier instead of two.
why: Facts 2 and 7: halves vertical bitlines and sense-amp connections per bit, about 1.4x tier density.

title: Self-rolling strained nanomembrane capacitors coil into cell-size towers
idea: [Box: rolled multilayer MIM charge | VCT | charge-share SA | BEOL | Si | strained bilayer deposition + sacrificial release, coarse ArF patches only] Deposit a strained TiN/high-k/TiN stack on a sacrificial film; releasing each patch makes it roll into a multi-turn Swiss-roll tube anchored on its pad, with capacitance set by film area and number of windings.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1): capacitance comes from deposited film area, not etched aspect ratio, so no high-AR mold and no EUV.

title: Capacitively coupled pads signal between laminated foils without vias
idea: Print 50x50 um pads facing each other across the 2 um adhesive between laminated foils and drive them with pulse signaling into a receiver, so tier-to-tier signals cross by AC coupling instead of drilled vias.
why: C=eA/d gives ~33 fF per pad pair against ~10 fF of receiver load, about 75% signal coupling, and pads tolerate the ~25 um registration of R2R lamination, removing via drilling, fill and their yield loss from foil stacks (the foil analogue of fact 6).

title: Zig-zag folded printed sheet: continuous traces cross folds, no vias
idea: Print one long sheet of 64 array panels separated by fold lines, encapsulate the traces at the bending neutral plane, and accordion-fold it into a 64-tier stack whose tier buses run continuously across every fold.
why: Bending strain e=y/R vanishes at the neutral plane, so 12 um films can fold at ~50 um radius without cracking traces; 64 tiers (above the 26-tier break-even, fact 2) need zero vias, zero bonding and zero alignment steps.

title: Defect-tolerant self-assembled lattice with a learned per-die address map
idea: IFR: 'the array patterns itself and defects do not matter.' Backward: form storage-node pillars by block-copolymer directed self-assembly (hexagonal cylinders at ~12-14 nm pitch guided by coarse DUV prepatterns), accept ~1e-4 dislocation rates, and electrically map each die at test into a compact defect-to-spare translation table in on-die fuses.
why: Litho capital (fact 4): replaces the capacitor-landing EUV layers; remapping makes DSA defect levels, which killed it before, acceptable.

title: Stacked-sensor sandwich: wordline drivers bonded above, sense amps below
idea: Three-layer stacked camera sensors showed a thinned die can be bonded on both faces; thin the DRAM array wafer to ~3 um, hybrid-bond a wordline-driver wafer to its top face and a sense-amp wafer to its bottom face, so wordlines exit upward and bitlines exit downward. The two peripheries never compete for one routing plane, the array die is ~100% cells, and both periphery wafers use logic processes.
why: Periphery and routing congestion (fact 7): array efficiency ~51% to ~95%, ~1.6x lower bit cost, and low-voltage logic periphery cuts energy (fact 10).

title: Anodic alumina pore lattice as mask-free 4F2 VCT array template
idea: [Box: MIM charge | coaxial IGZO VCT grown inside pores | charge-share SA | BEOL over CMOS | Si | Al anodization, no lithography for the cell lattice] Deposit Al over the bitlines, pre-texture it with a coarse ArF seed grid, and anodize to grow self-ordered hexagonal pores at ~25-40 nm pitch; ALD gate oxide, IGZO channel and storage contact coaxially inside each pore, with pore walls as the gate spacer.
why: Litho-bound capital (fact 4): the densest lattice comes from electrochemistry, with pitch set by anodization voltage; removes 2-3 EUV layers per wafer.

title: Tree-ring radial tiers: concentric shells in one wide hole
idea: Rotate the stacking axis from vertical to radial: deposit 10 concentric semiconductor/dielectric/conductor shells in a 400-nm hole, each ring the channel and storage node of its own cell. A conical chamfer etched at the hole top exposes each ring for contact, like tree rings on a slanted cut.
why: Tier count without tall stacks (fact 2): 10 cells per hole without 26+ deposited tiers, ~5x density per hole versus a one-cell vertical channel.

title: Array wafers from one US fab, periphery wafers from another, bonded
idea: Split DRAM across domestic fabs: array-only wafers (capacitors, access devices, few metals) at a US DRAM fab, periphery CMOS on depreciated 28-45 nm US logic/analog lines (e.g., TI Lehi, the former 3D XPoint fab), fused by wafer-to-wafer hybrid bonding on US soil.
why: Capital (fact 4) and periphery (fact 7): the costly DRAM fab spends all tools on bits (~2x bits per DRAM-fab wafer) while idle US logic capacity builds periphery; array die area per bit about -40%.

title: Face-to-face mirror bonding shares sense amps across two arrays
idea: Po: two chips stare at each other in a mirror. Build identical array wafers with sense-amp stripes on alternate mats, flip one and hybrid-bond face to face so every sense amp senses a bitline from its own array against the mirrored twin bitline across the bond as the reference, the SA stripes interleaving like a zipper.
why: Periphery 49% (fact 7): sense-amp area per bit halves and the reference line has matched capacitance, cutting open-bitline noise; ~15-20% die area per bit saved.

title: Sell retention-failed dies as never-refreshed ephemeral memory
idea: Po: the rejects are the product. Bin dies that fail the 64 ms retention spec but pass 4-8 ms and sell them as 'ephemeral memory' stacks for streaming workloads that must rewrite every buffer within a contractual window, enforced by a controller watchdog; refresh is never issued.
why: Supply: turns a top reject category into sellable bits (a few % more supply) at zero refresh power.

title: Smart-Cut donor reuse yields twenty single-crystal tiers per wafer
idea: TRIZ #34 Discarding and recovering: hydrogen-implant one premium 300 mm donor, bond and split a ~50 nm crystalline Si film onto the growing 3D stack, re-polish the donor, and repeat ~20 times so every tier has bulk-quality lateral channels. Bonding at <=400 C builds monolithic crystalline stacks without strained Si/SiGe superlattice epitaxy.
why: Fact 2 and resources: single-crystal lateral transistors (a key 3D blocker) without superlattice stress limits; ~20x less crucible-grown Si per tier.

title: Sculptor's lost-wax casting: inverse-opal sponge capacitor electrodes
idea: Self-assemble 30-50 nm silica spheres into a colloidal crystal as the wax, fill the gaps with TiN or Ru by ALD or electrodeposition, then dissolve the spheres in HF. Coat the interconnected metal sponge with ALD high-k and a top electrode.
why: Gives ~10x electrode area at ~10:1 height instead of 70:1 pillars (Fact 1), with no high-AR etch and no pillar collapse.

title: Extended-Core-Storage block tier: DRAM mats without column decoders
idea: Revive CDC 6600 Extended Core Storage, a huge bank used only for wide block moves: build a zero-EUV, >=18 nm DRAM die whose mats have no column decoders or column-select lines; every activation streams its full 8 KB row through a wide serializer to a CXL port for KV-cache, embedding and paging traffic.
why: Facts 4, 7 and 8: deletes column periphery (~10-15% of die), turns 128x overfetch into payload, and avoids EUV (~30% wafer-cost cut) for a cheap capacity tier.

title: Backside bitlines buried under a 4F2 vertical-channel array
idea: Limit: the front side may carry only capacitors and wordlines. After the 4F2 pillars are formed, flip-bond the wafer, thin it, and pattern bitlines on the exposed pillar bottoms from the backside. This removes bitline contacts and buried-bitline doping steps from the front.
why: Fact 4: true 4F2 (vs 6F2, about 1.5x density) with fewer front-side critical layers and lower bitline resistance.

title: Pastry chef's croissant lamination: stack-on-stack doubling of tiers
idea: Laminated dough doubles its layers with every fold. Make wafers with 8 monolithic tiers, hybrid-bond two face-to-face, thin and open vias; then bond 16-tier pairs to 16-tier pairs, mirroring orientation so the bitlines align.
why: Tier count doubles with each bond cycle: 3 cycles take 8 to 64 tiers, past the 26-tier break-even of Fact 2 without 64 sequential monolithic tiers.

title: Two-scale stacking: 32 monolithic tiers per wafer times eight bonded wafers
idea: Combine nm-scale monolithic tiers with um-scale wafer bonding: build 32-tier 3D arrays per wafer, thin each to 5 um, and hybrid-bond eight wafers with one inter-wafer via per mat at 1-um pitch, reaching 256 tiers without any 256-tier etch.
why: High-AR etch and tier yield (fact 2): yield compounds over 32 tiers instead of 256, giving 256-tier density at 32-tier process risk.

title: DRAM tiers and NAND tiers sharing one CMOS-under-array stack
idea: Combine a 3D DRAM tier block and a 3D NAND tier block above the same CMOS-under-array die, sharing staircases and page buffers, so pages migrate between DRAM and NAND tiers internally at TB/s without crossing an I/O pin.
why: Do DRAM's job with less DRAM: cold pages demote in-die, so a system needs maybe 30-50% fewer DRAM bits; data movement (fact 5) for swap traffic nearly eliminated.

title: Soviet engineer converts the tractor plant: NAND lines making DRAM
idea: Like a tractor factory retooled for tanks, a 10-person design team writes 1-2 mask deltas and recipe changes so an existing 3D NAND line (staircase, channel holes, tier stack) builds a vertical 2T0C gain cell. An ALD oxide-semiconductor liner replaces the poly-Si channel in the hole. The fab runs it as foundry lots.
why: Gets 3D DRAM onto already-depreciated 100+ tier tools (Facts 2, 4: depreciation is ~55% of wafer cost) without anyone building a new fab.

title: Dating app: wafer-map matchmaking before wafer-to-wafer HBM stacking
idea: A dating app pairs compatible profiles: probe-test each DRAM wafer, store its defect map, and use an assignment solver to choose which wafers and which rotation (0/90/180/270) to bond wafer-to-wafer so bad sites land on bad sites. Dice the pre-bonded stacks into HBM core blocks with the standard HBM interface.
why: HBM yield (fact 6) and bonding throughput: W2W cost with yield loss near known-good-die D2W; claim stacking cost -30% and +10-15 points good-stack yield.

title: Bonded diamond spreader tiers replace silicon spacers under stacked DRAM
idea: Substitute passive silicon spacers in memory-on-logic stacks with bonded polycrystalline CVD diamond tiers (CH4/H2 growth, mechanical thinning, O2-plasma activation, laser-drilled Cu vias) between GPU and stacked DRAM, spreading heat ~10x better than Si so DRAM can sit directly on compute.
why: Data movement (fact 5): DRAM-on-logic cuts ~3-4 pJ/bit (HBM) to <0.5; diamond keeps DRAM <85 C so refresh rate does not double (fact 3); no fluorinated coolants.

title: Qubit-control superconducting wordlines shrink sub-wordline driver strips
idea: Control memory for 4 K quantum computers can use NbTiN wordlines with no resistive RC, so one sub-wordline driver can span 8x more cells; at 77 K the same floorplan uses copper or YBCO-strapped wordlines whose resistivity drops 5-7x. Re-floorplan the mats with 4-8x longer wordline segments so the driver strips that tile the array shrink proportionally.
why: Periphery takes ~49% of the die (fact 7): cutting sub-wordline driver strips 4x frees ~8-12% of die area and gives a cold-memory floorplan that generalizes.

title: Self-latching lateral thyristor in each superlattice tier
idea: TRIZ #25 Self-service: dope each tier's lateral Si strip in situ as p+/n/p/n+ during epitaxy and gate the p-base with the vertical wordline, so the cell latches itself into a regenerative ON or blocking OFF state. It holds that state on ~pA standby current with no refresh and no capacitor, and reads with a large current ratio.
why: Fact 3 and 8: no refresh (saves 16-33% idle power), non-destructive read (no restore energy), ~6F2 per tier, stackable to 32+ tiers.

title: Piezo-resonant tier select replaces 3D staircase contacts
idea: Piezoelectric effect: each tier of a 3D DRAM stack gets a thin AlScN bulk-acoustic resonator in its local wordline-driver enable path, with a tier-unique film thickness (tier-unique resonance). One shared vertical RF drive line carries the frequency of the target tier, so only that tier's resonator builds enough piezo voltage to enable its drivers.
why: Removes the staircase and per-tier decoders that grow with 26+ tiers (periphery ~49%, fact 7; 3D blocker, fact 2); claim 30-50% less tier-addressing area and one shared via instead of N staircase contacts.

title: Inside-out cell: concentric shells built around one etched hole
idea: IFR: 'one hole builds every tier with no lateral patterning.' Backward: etch one hole through a 100-layer wordline-plane/sacrificial stack, recess each sacrificial layer by a self-limiting digital etch, and fill each annular cavity as nested shells (outer plate, high-k, storage node, oxide-semiconductor channel) so each tier forms a ring cell around the central vertical bitline, gated by its own wordline plane and sized only by film thickness.
why: 3D blocker and litho capital (facts 2, 4): ~1 critical mask per 100 tiers, putting DRAM on the 3D NAND cost curve.

title: Hydrogen anneal reshapes hole arrays into stacked silicon-on-nothing tiers
idea: Etch rows of deep holes with periodically modulated diameter by cycled DRIE, then anneal at ~1100 C in H2 in a hydrogen-capable university furnace: Si surface migration closes each row into a stack of flat buried voids, leaving thin single-crystal Si membranes between them as device tiers and the voids as capacitor or isolation cavities.
why: Multiple crystalline lateral-transistor tiers from a bulk wafer using only i-line litho, DRIE and a furnace (fact 2), no epi reactor or bonder; an ideal 4-8-tier lateral-cell testbed.

title: Photo-electrochemical macropore etching for 150:1 silicon capacitor trenches
idea: [Box: Si trench charge | VCT | charge-share SA | capacitor-first in substrate | n-type Si | backside-illuminated anodization in HF] Seed pits with a coarse ArF or DSA pattern, then grow capacitor holes into n-Si by backside-illuminated electrochemical etching that propagates straight at AR 150+ with no plasma; line with ALD high-k and fill with TiN.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1): AR beyond 115 without plasma etchers or EUV; wet tooling is cheap and U.S.-buildable. Sub-100 nm pore pitch is the key risk.

title: Eliminate the big monolithic die: fluidically self-assembled mat-lets
idea: Fabricate 0.5-1 mm2 DRAM mat-lets (array plus local SA), test and bin them, then pour them onto a logic wafer where shape-matched recesses and capillary forces seat them before a batch bond.
why: Yield and capital: known-good small tiles avoid large-die yield loss, and mat-lets can come from many small older fabs, including U.S. lines.

title: Reactor neutron-transmutation-doped donor wafers for transferred array tiers
idea: Power-device makers dope silicon in a nuclear reactor, turning Si-30 into phosphorus with near-perfect uniformity; NTD-dope the donor wafers whose thin layers are transferred to form junctionless n-type channel tiers, so channel doping is fixed before transfer. Array implants and their xenon or argon plasma flood guns are skipped.
why: Removes array doping implants and rare-gas flood-gun use, and eliminates CZ striations and implant dose drift; ~10-20% tighter Vt spread trims the leakage tail (fact 3).

title: Minify TSVs to zero: print staircase stack interconnects
idea: Offset 16 commodity bare LPDDR dies into a staircase and aerosol-jet print fine sidewall traces down each step to a substrate, giving a tall, TSV-free stack built in a packaging lab for about $300k.
why: HBM TSV tax: more capacity per package without the 3x wafer area or the 20-30% TSV yield hit, using dies that can be bought today.

title: Archaeal tetraether-style Cu grains spanning the hybrid bond interface
idea: Hyperthermophilic archaea survive >100 C with tetraether lipids that span the whole membrane instead of two stacked leaflets; analogously, use (111) nanotwinned Cu bond pads and a ~200 C anneal that drives grain growth across the interface so single grains span both dies, erasing the bond line where voids nucleate under 125 C electro- and thermomigration.
why: 125 C/10-yr 3D bond reliability: removing the interface plane removes the dominant void site, targeting >10x EM lifetime and enabling <1 um-pitch bonding in automotive-grade memory stacks.

title: Eliminate the capacitor hole: bottom-up nanowire capacitor electrodes
idea: Instead of etching a mold, grow a conductive nanowire (doped Si or silicide, using a CMOS-safe Al or Sn catalyst) vapour-liquid-solid straight up from each storage node to AR 200:1, then wrap it in ALD high-k and plate.
why: Water and charge wall: no mold deposition, hole etch, polymer clean or dip-out, so most capacitor wet steps vanish; free-standing high-AR wires give ~2x Cs.

title: Atomically thin channel tiers: 250 tiers in the same etch depth
idea: Worse: make each tier 50-70 nm thick so 100 tiers already need a 6 um etch. Flip: shrink tier pitch to ~20 nm by using 1-3 nm channels (ALD In2O3-class oxide or CVD MoS2), 5 nm gate dielectric and thin metal gates, so ~250 tiers fit into the 5-6 um depth that 3D NAND already etches.
why: ~3x more tiers per unit etch depth: 250 tiers at ~60F2 per tier-cell is ~35 nm2/bit (>10x even with 50% array efficiency) at an unchanged etch budget (facts 2, 4).

title: In-tier thin-film decoders eliminate the 3D wordline staircase
idea: Inverts 'tiers are selected through an edge staircase of contacts.' Each tier carries its own poly-Si TFT tier/row decoder made in the same step as its access devices, and a few vertical broadcast lines carry the tier address, so no staircase etch or per-tier contact is needed.
why: Facts 2 and 7: staircase plus contacts consume ~10-15% area and many masks at 100+ tiers; removing it decouples tier count from staircase area.

title: Minify tunnel oxide to 1.5 nm: leaky 3D NAND as DRAM
idea: Take a 200+ layer charge-trap 3D NAND flow and thin the tunnel oxide to about 1.5 nm, so cells write by direct tunneling in about 10-50 ns and leak in about 1-10 s. The controller refreshes them like DRAM, and direct tunneling may avoid hot-carrier wear.
why: Reuses the cheapest per-bit 3D process in the world for working memory, with density about 5-10x DRAM. Endurance is unproven.

title: MicroLED mass transfer of known-good DRAM micro-tiles
idea: Adopt microLED display mass transfer: make DRAM arrays as 200 um micro-tiles on a dense array wafer, test and map them, then stamp-transfer only good tiles, thousands per stroke, onto a periphery/logic wafer with hybrid-bond landing pads, assembling dies from perfect tiles.
why: Yield and HBM tax (fact 6): tile-level known-good assembly recovers the 20-30% stack yield loss and lets the array wafer run a stripped-down process; claims ~25% lower cost per bit.

title: Trilogy wafer-scale fixed with bondable patch-tile repair sites
idea: Gene Amdahl's Trilogy failed because wafer-scale defects could not be fixed after the wafer was built. Lay out a wafer-scale DRAM slab with a grid of empty landing sites over each region. After test, or later in a service depot, a known-good DRAM tile is bonded over any dead region and the router remaps it.
why: Wafer-scale economics for packaging and I/O energy (facts 5, 6) without the yield risk. The slab stays repairable over a 10-year life.

title: Nitrogen: aluminum-nitride inter-tier heat spreaders hold retention in hot stacks
idea: Use sputtered/ALD polycrystalline AlN (30-100 W/mK vs 1.4 for SiO2) as every third inter-tier dielectric and as the bonding dielectric of memory-on-logic stacks, with AlN-filled dummy holes acting as vertical thermal pillars to the lid.
why: Leakage roughly doubles every ~10 C, so 3D DRAM over hot logic loses retention (fact 3); cutting stack temperature rise by 10-15 C halves refresh energy and lets DRAM sit directly on accelerators (fact 5).

title: Convert depreciated 3D NAND lines into stacked-DRAM tier fabs
idea: From a first-principles count of process steps, a 3D DRAM tier stack is mostly deposition, high-aspect-ratio etch and replacement-metal steps, the same tool mix as 3D NAND; retrofit NAND lines idled by oversupply with DRAM-specific modules (capacitor dielectric, anneal) instead of building greenfield fabs.
why: Capital intensity and time: reusing ~60-70% of installed tools cuts capex per wafer start ~2-3x and lead time from 3-5 years to ~1-2 years, attacking the $15B+ fab barrier.

title: Self-rolling nanomembrane capacitors instead of etched 70:1 pillars
idea: Inverts 'tall capacitors must be etched downward.' Deposit a flat strained bilayer carrying electrode/dielectric/electrode, undercut a sacrificial layer and let built-in stress roll it into a multi-turn Swiss-roll capacitor standing over its transistor, giving plate area equal to AR>100 from flat films.
why: Fact 1: breaks the capacitor charge wall without high-AR etch; ~2-3x Cs per footprint if roll diameters reach <100 nm.

title: Big old capacitor, many levels: 16-level charge in 180-nm cells
idea: Turn the coarse scale into resolution: 180-nm trench cells hold ~30-40 fF, enough charge for 16 levels about 60 mV apart, so a shared successive-approximation sense amp per mat reads 4 bits per cell. A 1990s-geometry cell stores 4x the bits.
why: Density without litho (fact 4): 4x bits per cell area by spending the surplus charge of older, larger cells.

title: Sun proximity communication revived as solder-free, demountable DRAM stacks
idea: Sun's capacitive proximity communication died on alignment and Oracle's acquisition. Carry die-to-die signals on capacitive pads in a clamped DRAM stack, deliver power through spring pins, and align dies with etched V-groove-and-ball kinematic mounts. With no solder or underfill, a failed die is unclamped and swapped, and dies separate cleanly for reuse at end of life.
why: Ends the HBM yield tax (fact 6) because a bad die is replaced rather than the stack scrapped. Repairable and fully recyclable.

title: Corrugated cardboard flutes: tiers deposited over sinusoidal templates
idea: Borrowed from corrugated board, where a fluted middle sheet multiplies stiffness and surface: etch a shallow sinusoidal corrugation into the base, then deposit the 3D tier stack so every horizontal tier and its lateral capacitor follow the wave, multiplying electrode area without deep etches.
why: Lateral 3D capacitors gain ~2.5-3x area (facts 1-2) using only shallow features, e.g. Cs ~1.5 to ~4 fF per horizontal cell.

title: Corrugated capacitor walls from multilayer selective recess
idea: Worse: etch smooth cylinder walls so electrode area grows only with height. Flip: etch capacitor holes through an alternating oxide/nitride (or Si/SiGe) mold and selectively recess every other layer before electrode deposition, giving fin-like corrugated walls that multiply area 2-3x at the same aspect ratio.
why: Breaks the capacitor charge wall without AR 115 or k 70 (fact 1): ~5 fF at AR ~30-40, which also eases mold collapse.

title: Farmer's alternating furrows: half-pitch-staggered tiers share vertical bitlines
idea: Farmers offset alternate furrows. In a horizontal-cell 3D DRAM, shift every odd tier by half a cell pitch so each vertical bitline pillar zippers between cells on its left and right as it climbs, serving two columns.
why: Halves the number of vertical bitline holes, or doubles their pitch, at the same bit density. This relieves the hardest 3D etch and cuts bitline coupling (Fact 2).

title: Single-exposure ArF array, density made up by tier count
idea: [Box: lateral 1T1C | IGZO | standard SA | monolithic 3D | Si | single-exposure ArF immersion only (>=38 nm half-pitch), no multipatterning] Freeze lateral pitch at what one ArF immersion exposure can print and make tier count the only scaling knob, co-designing a wide-pitch cell (longer lateral capacitor, relaxed contacts) so mask count stays almost flat from 32 to 200 tiers.
why: Litho-bound capital (fact 4): no EUV and no SAQP, so depreciation share falls as bits grow through cheap deposition/etch cycles.

title: Thermonastic capacitors: permittivity rises with heat to offset leakage
idea: Like flowers and pinecones that open in response to heat, tune the 3D cell dielectric to a ferroelectric-paraelectric transition near 140-150 C (e.g. Sn/Zr-doped BaTiO3 or a Zr-rich HfZrO superlattice) so permittivity climbs ~2-3x from 25 to 125 C, raising stored charge just as leakage accelerates.
why: Retention scales with Cs*dV/Ileak: a temperature-rising Cs partly cancels the leakage rise, cutting the 125 C refresh penalty ~2-3x at no area cost.

title: Rotate the page vertical: one cell per tier, 64-bit activation
idea: In 3D DRAM, reverse the activation axis: a short vertical word-pillar gates exactly one cell in each of 64 tiers, and each tier senses on its own horizontal bitline, so one activation opens a 64-bit vertical column instead of an 8 kb row.
why: Overfetch and row hammer (facts 8,9): activation energy per useful bit drops ~50-100x; an aggressor pillar disturbs only its few neighbors, not a whole row.

title: Pillar-word organization: one vertical wordline opens exactly one word
idea: TRIZ #1 Segmentation: segment the page vertically instead of horizontally. In a 64-tier capacitorless stack, one vertical wordline pillar gates exactly one cell per tier, and each tier has its own short bitline and latch, so one activation delivers a single 64-bit word up the column.
why: Fact 8 and 9: overfetch drops from 128x to ~1x (energy per useful random bit ~5-10x lower) and only 64 cells are disturbed per activation.

title: Grounded shield film between every wordline tier, deposition-defined
idea: In horizontal-wordline 3D stacks, insert a 5-10 nm grounded metal or doped-poly film between adjacent wordline tiers so aggressor field lines terminate on ground instead of on the victim's storage node or channel.
why: Row hammer (fact 9) is driven by capacitive coupling and carrier injection across wordline spacing; in 3D the vertical spacer costs one deposition, not lithographic area, so coupling can drop >10x, raising flip thresholds from ~1k toward >50k activations and retiring TRR/RFM bandwidth overhead.

title: Video P-frames: delta bitlines swing only when data changes
idea: Video codecs send only what changed between frames; skip bitline equalization between successive activations in a subarray and sense each new row against the bitline's previous value with a dummy-cell reference, so a bitline toggles only where the new row differs, while the controller orders correlated rows back to back.
why: Bitline energy proportional to Hamming distance (fact 8): for streaming tensors and KV pages with ~10% bit toggles, claims up to ~10x lower bitline energy.

title: Self-stratifying paint: one coat separates into fifty tier layers
idea: Borrowed from self-stratifying industrial coatings that split into primer and topcoat in one application: spin a block-copolymer plus metal-oxide-precursor blend that phase-separates into ~50 parallel lamellae, then UV-ozone convert and anneal it into alternating conductive-oxide and insulating-oxide tiers for a vertical gain-cell stack.
why: One coat-and-bake replaces ~100 CVD steps for a 50-tier stack, aiming at ~100x lower stack cost; trade-off: oxide-electrode resistance limits access to hundreds of ns.

title: Janus pillar: bitline at the waist, cells at both ends
idea: Limit: capacitor height capped at 300 nm per side. A 4F2 vertical pillar has a buried bitline contacting its middle. The upper half has its own gate and frontside capacitor. After wafer flip and bond, the lower half gets a second gate and a backside capacitor, so the pillar holds two independent cells.
why: Facts 1 and 4: 2F2 per bit with two short, low-AR capacitors instead of one 75:1 pillar, about 3x density at the same F.

title: Coaxial grounded sleeve around vertical bitlines replaces bare pillars
idea: In vertical-bitline 3D DRAM, substitute the bare bitline pillar with a coax: ALD grounded TiN sleeve / Al2O3 / inner bitline, the sleeve opened only at each tier's access-transistor window by a self-aligned lateral recess, converting BL-to-BL coupling into fixed ground capacitance.
why: Neighbor-coupling noise caps tiers per sense amp in VBL designs; shielding allows ~2x more tiers per SA (taller pillars), roughly halving SA count (periphery, fact 7).

title: Hearing-aid origami: fold one thinned DRAM strip into eight-high stack
idea: Hearing aids fit electronics by folding flex circuits; thin a strip of 8 DRAM die segments to ~10 um so the silicon flexes, pattern polymer-copper hinge interconnects between segments, and fold it accordion-style into a stack bonded with thin adhesive. The fold edges carry hundreds of wires per mm and replace TSVs for capacity-oriented stacks.
why: HBM TSV tax (fact 6): TSV keep-out area and TSV yield loss (20-30%) removed, and stacking becomes a back-end assembly step.

title: Staktek package stacking reborn as blade-stacked, edge-contact DRAM dies
idea: Staktek's stacked packages lost to TSVs because their flex leads were coarse. Mount each thinned DRAM die on a thin carrier blade with fine edge contacts, and slide the blades into a compression-contact backplane next to the processor. Any blade can be pulled and replaced.
why: Replaces TSVs (fact 6) with edge contacts and makes each die serviceable and recyclable, at density near HBM with no TSV yield loss.

title: Coaxial cable: polymer-lined annular TSVs shrink keep-out to near zero
idea: A coax cushions its core with a soft dielectric: make each HBM TSV an annular Cu ring around a Si core with a 1 um BCB or parylene liner that absorbs the CTE stress, so transistors and mats can sit within ~1 um of the via instead of 5-10 um. TSV count and the HBM interface stay the same.
why: HBM TSV tax (fact 6): keep-out area -80%, recovering ~5-8% of core-die area per bit.

title: Millefiori glass canes: thermally draw a macro preform into nanocells
idea: Borrowed from millefiori glass and optical-fiber preform drawing: assemble a centimeter-scale preform whose cross-section holds semiconducting glass, metal and dielectric regions forming a cell row, thermally draw it ~10,000x into kilometers of fiber, then slice, bundle and bond cross-sections as arrays with no lithography.
why: Pattern is made once at mm scale and replicated at km/hour; capital per bit ~1/100 of a fab; trade-offs: chalcogenide/oxide-glass devices, ~1 us access, coarse yield.

title: Tantalum capacitor powder metallurgy: sintered nanosponge storage electrode
idea: Adapted from solid tantalum capacitor anodes (pressed, sintered powder with enormous internal area): fill each storage-node cavity with a sintered TiN/Ru nanoparticle sponge, then ALD high-k and the plate electrode through its open pores.
why: Surface enhancement ~5-10x per volume lets a 20:1 cavity match a 70:1 pillar (fact 1), relieving high-AR etch and pattern collapse.

title: Lithium-moved Schottky barrier makes selector-free cross-point tiers
idea: Ion migration: a field-driven Li-ion shift at a LixTiO2/metal interface moves a Schottky barrier, so the same junction stores a non-volatile resistance state and rectifies current. Self-rectifying cells allow 4F2 BEOL cross-point tiers with no separate selector layer.
why: Gives 4F2 stacked non-volatile cells without a transistor or selector (facts 2 and 4); claim 2x fewer layers per tier than 1S1R cross-point and cheap BEOL stacking.

title: Origami artist's accordion: dies folded on flexible hinges
idea: Leave N memory dies in a row on a wafer strip and thin it to 20 um. Laser-ablate the silicon between dies so polyimide/Cu flex hinges carrying the shared bus remain, then fold the strip accordion-style in a jig into an N-high stack.
why: No TSVs, no die-to-die bonding and no interposer. The bus runs through the hinges, and a 10-person team can build an 8-high stack with thinning, a laser and a fixture (Fact 6).

title: Sawtooth multilayer mold replaces smooth capacitor cylinder walls
idea: Substitute the uniform oxide capacitor mold with a 10 nm-period SiO2/SiN nanolaminate; after the hole etch, recess SiN laterally ~5 nm in hot phosphoric acid so the ALD TiN/ZrO2/TiN conforms to a sawtooth sidewall with ~1.7x surface area, a deterministic successor to 1990s hemispherical-grain poly.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1): Cs 5 -> 8 fF at today's 60:1 AR, equivalent to AR ~100 without the harder etch; corrugations stiffen pillars against leaning.

title: 1T-nC cell: one access transistor, eight plate-addressed capacitors
idea: Inverts 'one transistor serves one capacitor.' Hang n capacitors off a single storage-node transistor, each with its own plate line; pulsing one plate couples only that capacitor's charge onto the node for sensing, as in 1T-nC FeRAM but with linear-dielectric charge.
why: Facts 3-4: transistor count and leakage paths per bit fall ~n-fold; capacitors stacked vertically over one transistor give 3D without lateral transistors.
